About the Science and AI Team 
 The Science and AI team is at the heart of Maki People. It builds the science and AI behind our platform, from job analysis and assessments to AI interviews and predicting performance. Led by our Head of Science, Aiden Loe, and working closely with our COO, Paul-Louis Caylar, the team brings together business psychologists, psychometricians and AI scientists. Together, they make sure every hiring decision on our platform is accurate, consistent and fair. 
 As Maki grows, the Science and AI team’s job is to show, with evidence, that our approach leads to better hiring decisions.
 About the Role 
 The AI Research Scientist works at the intersection of AI, psychometrics and research, ensuring that Maki’s automated scoring systems are scientifically robust, fair, and continuously improving.
 1. Evaluating and testing LLMs for scoring 
 Assess the accuracy and reliability of LLMs used for automated scoring, such as structured grids, job-specific skills and multilingual proficiency (written and spoken).
 Benchmark closed- and open-source models across assessment types and languages.
 Test robustness to prompt variation, input noise and adversarial behaviour such as prompt injection.
 Explore prompt engineering and model optimisation, and recommend which models and prompts go into production.
 2. Building our own scoring models 
 Move our scoring onto self-hosted open-weight models, and fine-tune them on expert-rated data where they can beat frontier models.
 Check every model switch keeps accuracy, reliability and fairness at least as good as today's.
 3. Comparing AI with human judgement, and calibrating psychometric models 
 Design studies that compare AI scores with expert ratings, against both individual experts and expert averages, to establish agreement and validity.
 Develop hybrid scoring pipelines with engineering that combine human oversight with AI scoring.
 Evaluate and calibrate psychometric models for validity and comparability across populations and test forms.
 4. Bias and fairness analysis 
 Detect and analyse bias in AI-generated and psychometric scores across demographic groups, including subgroup analysis.
 Apply mitigation techniques such as reweighting and calibration without losing model performance.
 Contribute to fairness dashboards and compliance documentation that support transparent model governance.
 5. Predictive analytics and performance insights 
 Model the relationship between candidate scores and job performance and retention, using large assessment and performance datasets.
 Develop and test models that estimate success probabilities or identify behavioural and linguistic predictors of performance.
 Work with data science, implementation and customer success teams to turn findings into recommendations for clients and colleagues.
 6. Research output 
 Publish reports, papers and conference presentations, internal and external.
 Explain technical findings clearly to non-technical colleagues and clients.
 As one of Maki People's early employees, you'll help shape the team's future. 
 Our Ideal Candidate 
 Required 
 PhD or MSc in machine learning, computational linguistics, data science or psychology.
 A track record of publications, such as peer-reviewed papers or conference papers.
 Hands-on experience evaluating LLMs: designing benchmarks, measuring agreement with human raters, and testing consistency and robustness of model output.
 Experience testing AI-driven decisions for fairness and bias.
 Proficiency in Python or R, with experience in statistical analysis.
 Clear communication of results to scientific and business audiences.
 Preferred 
 Experience with NLP techniques for automated scoring.
 Experience fine-tuning language models, for example with LoRA.
 Experience working with cloud databases and large datasets.
 Working knowledge of psychometric concepts such as reliability, validity and IRT, and how they apply to assessment design and validation.
 Working knowledge of ethical AI, data governance and compliance, such as the EU AI Act.
 Experience working with engineering, product and content teams.

 Stage 4 - Executive interview (45 min)
 Stage 5 - Deep-dive technical interview (60 min)

Our Mission
 At Circus (Xetra: CA1), headquartered in Munich, we are pioneering global developments in on-demand autonomous food production. Everything from creation to production and operation – enabled by seamlessly integrated cutting-edge robotics and transformative AI technology.
Our foundation rests in the extensive developments of groundbreaking robotics driven by artificial intelligence, previously the missing link in achieving true autonomous food automation. This is the moment for a new status quo: Just as autonomous driving will disrupt how we build cities, organize our days, and live our lives, so will we shift our whole reality around food.
Our Team is backing a paradigm shift in one of humanity’s most important sectors with the sharpest minds in Robotics, AI, Engineering and Culinary, collaborating closely with industry-leading partners to revolutionize every aspect of the food service experience.
Join us as we forge ahead, crafting a future where the art of cooking and the science of technology converge to create a world that thinks differently about food than it has for thousands of years – a world where food means something new.
 About The Role
 Design the mechanical modules of the next generations of our robotic kitchens and take them from first sketch to serial production. You will own entire modules and subsystems, from concept through prototyping and validation to release, and see your designs run in real commercial kitchens. You will work across Robotics, Electrical, Software, Culinary and Operations, and help shape how we engineer as we move from innovation to commercial scale.
 Your Daily Business
 Own one or more modules end to end, from early concepts and prototypes through validation and release.
 Design, test and release mechanical components and subsystems for our robotic kitchen.
 Drive DFM with suppliers and partners and manage the industrialization of your parts and assemblies.
 Work with Robotics, Electrical, Culinary, Production and Operations to deliver robust designs that scale.
 Improve existing modules for performance, manufacturability and cost.
 Write technical documentation, test plans and risk assessments, including FMEA and operability analysis.
 Help define our internal engineering standards and development processes.
 Base Qualifications
 A Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
 2–5 years designing mechanical systems and assemblies for complex mechatronic products, ideally for serial production.
 Strong parametric CAD skills (SolidWorks preferred) and the ability to produce manufacturing-ready technical drawings.
 Hands-on knowledge of manufacturing processes such as sheet metal, welding, 3D printing, injection molding and casting.
 A proven track record in prototyping, testing and validating mechanical systems, in both product innovation and production scaling.
 An AI-native way of working: AI tools are a natural part of your daily work, from exploring design concepts and running analyses to writing documentation.
 Familiarity with relevant norms, compliance standards and safety/risk analysis.
 A structured, solution-driven and entrepreneurial way of working, plus excellent English.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience with flow simulation and optimization of HVLS fans, axial fans, coolers, exhausts and air circulators.
 Experience in food-tech or commercial hardware.
 Kinematic design experience.
 German language skills.
 Our Offer
 Competitive Compensation: Competitive compensation package with stock option opportunities for full-time employees.
 Work-Life Balance: Regular team events, hybrid work setup, 2 months/year remote work (Worcation), unlimited vacation days, and a corporate pension plan.
 Personal Development: Personal budget for training, in-house trainings, and growth opportunities in a fast-paced environment.
 Mobility: Monthly budget for mobility or other expenses, a subsidized Dance Mobility Subscription for E-Bike/E-Moped, and bike leasing via JobRad.
 Well-Being: Discounted Urban Sports Club membership and Wellhub for a variety of well-being offerings.

items.jobTitle: Softwareentwickler Embedded Vision & FPGA (m/w/d) in Aalen
items.jobDescription:
Embedded Software, Linux, Bildverarbeitung und anspruchsvolle Kundenprojekte sind genau dein Ding?
Dann werde Teil unseres Entwicklerteams in Aalen und gestalte innovative Embedded-Lösungen von der Konzeption bis zur Inbetriebnahme.
 Mit deiner Arbeit entstehen Lösungen, die weltweit in Industrie-, Medizin- und Sicherheitstechnik zum Einsatz kommen und höchste Anforderungen an Zuverlässigkeit und Qualität erfüllen.
 hema ist eines der erfolgreichsten Embedded-Vision-Design-Labs Europas. Wir entwickeln innovative Lösungen für Kunden aus Industrie-, Medizin- und Sicherheitstechnik und verbinden dabei modernste Technologien mit langjähriger Engineering-Expertise.
Als Familienunternehmen denken wir langfristig. Unsere Entscheidungen orientieren sich nicht an Quartalszahlen, sondern an nachhaltigem Wachstum, langfristigen Kundenbeziehungen und einem Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen gerne bleiben.
Uns verbindet die Leidenschaft, technologisch anspruchsvolle Lösungen zu entwickeln. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig, lernen kontinuierlich dazu und schaffen gemeinsam Außergewöhnliches.
Diese Aufgaben warten auf dich
Als Softwareentwickler Embedded Systems (m/w/d) konzipierst und realisierst du kundenspezifische Anwendungen für Embedded Systeme. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf Bild- und Videoverarbeitung sowie der hardwarenahen Entwicklung im FPGA-Umfeld.
Dabei arbeitest du unter anderem mit C/C++, C#, Python, Linux, PetaLinux sowie FPGA-basierten Embedded-Systemen.
 Zu Deinen Aufgaben Gehören
 Entwicklung kundenspezifischer Softwarelösungen im Bereich Bild- und Videoverarbeitung
 Test, Integration und Verifikation der entwickelten Software im Gesamtsystem
 Design und Weiterentwicklung von Library-Komponenten mit Schwerpunkt Bildverarbeitung und Kommunikationsschnittstellen
 Integration und Anpassung von Linux auf FPGA-basierten Embedded-Systemen unter Verwendung von PetaLinux
 Definition, Implementierung und Dokumentation von Software-Schnittstellen
 Hardwarenahe Programmierung von FPGA-Schnittstellen in C/C++, C# sowie Python unter Linux
 Was du mitbringst
 Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Elektrotechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
 Mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Embedded-Softwareentwicklung
 Sehr gute Kenntnisse in C und C++
 Sehr gute Kenntnisse in der hardwarenahen Softwareentwicklung
 Sehr gute Erfahrung im Umgang mit Linux-basierten Embedded-Systemen
 Idealerweise Kenntnisse in C#, Python, FPGA-basierten Systemen sowie PetaLinux
 Erfahrung im Bereich Bildverarbeitung oder industrieller Kommunikationsschnittstellen von Vorteil
 Analytische und strukturierte Arbeitsweise sowie ein ausgeprägtes technisches Verständnis
 Eigeninitiative, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Freude an technologischen Herausforderungen
 Teamgeist sowie die Motivation, gemeinsam innovative Lösungen zu entwickeln
 Wichtig ist uns nicht, dass du jeden einzelnen Punkt erfüllst. Entscheidend sind deine fachliche Kompetenz, deine Motivation und die Bereitschaft, gemeinsam mit uns an anspruchsvollen Technologien zu arbeiten.
 Unsicher, ob die Stelle passt?
Du erkennst dich in der Anzeige wieder, erfüllst aber nicht jeden einzelnen Punkt?
Dann bewirb dich trotzdem.
Wenn du beruflich im Bereich Embedded Software zuhause bist und Lust auf spannende Technologieprojekte hast, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.
Unser Arbeitsumfeld - Innovation und Verlässlichkeit
Für unsere Kunden sind wir kompetente Partner auf Augenhöhe. Deshalb haben wir einen hohen Anspruch an die Qualität unserer Arbeit.
 Wir Setzen Auf
 Eigenverantwortung
 Teamarbeit
 Partizipation
 Individuelle Förderung
 Kontinuierliches Lernen
 Ein familiärer, offener und wertschätzender Umgang miteinander ist für uns selbstverständlich. Wir entwickeln uns stetig weiter und erwarten die Bereitschaft, Neues zu lernen und gemeinsam zu wachsen.
Wenn du dich in einem mittelständischen Familienunternehmen wohler fühlst als in der Anonymität eines Großkonzerns, passt du hervorragend zu uns.
Deine Vorteile - Mehr als nur ein Job!
 Langfristige Perspektive – Unbefristeter Vertrag in einem zukunftsorientierten Unternehmen
 Flexibilität & Work-Life-Balance – Moderne Arbeitsmodelle, die sich deinem Leben anpassen
 Gezielte Weiterbildung – Individuelle Förderung und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten
 Attraktive Zusatzleistungen – Urlaubs- & Weihnachtsgeld, Firmenfahrrad-Leasing, Zuschüsse zur Kinderbetreuung, betriebliche Altersvorsorge und mehr
 Effiziente Prozesse – Klare Zuständigkeiten und direkte Kommunikationswege
 So geht es weiter
 Du bewirbst dich direkt online über unseren Bewerbungsbutton.
 Wir prüfen deine Unterlagen zeitnah.
 In einem ersten Telefonat lernen wir uns kennen und sprechen offen über Erwartungen, Aufgaben und Rahmenbedingungen.
 Im persönlichen Gespräch erhältst du Einblicke in unsere Projekte, Technologien und das Team.
 Wenn es für beide Seiten passt, freuen wir uns darauf, gemeinsam die Zukunft zu gestalten.
 Vertraulichkeit garantiert!
Falls du dich aktuell in einem ungekündigten Arbeitsverhältnis befindest, behandeln wir deine Bewerbung selbstverständlich mit höchster Vertraulichkeit.
Telefoninterviews und persönliche Gespräche sind bei Bedarf auch außerhalb der üblichen Geschäftszeiten möglich.
Vergütung & Rahmenbedingungen
Wir wissen, wie wichtig transparente Erwartungen sind.
Deshalb sprechen wir bereits im ersten Telefonat offen über Gehalt, Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten und alle organisatorischen Rahmenbedingungen der Position.
Die Vergütung orientiert sich an deiner Erfahrung, deinen Qualifikationen und deiner zukünftigen Verantwortung bei uns.
Klingt das gut? Dann bewirb dich jetzt.
Wir freuen uns auf dich!

Unsere induktiven Metallsensoren und Hyperspektralkameras arbeiten in Sortier- und Recyclinganlagen auf der ganzen Welt, viele davon seit Jahren. Damit das so bleibt, braucht es jemanden, der diese Hardware wirklich kennt: neue Designs müssen entwickelt und alte Designs überarbeitet werden, Bauteile werden abgekündigt, Auffälligkeiten aus Fertigung oder Feld wollen bis zur Ursache verstanden werden.
 Unsere Strategie setzt stark auf Software und Komplettlösungen. Die Sensorhardware bleibt dabei das Fundament. In dieser Rolle bist du Ansprechperson für Elektronik. Du arbeitest eigenständig und eng mit unseren POs, dem TechLead Hardware, dem Mechanical Engineer, dem Firmware-Team, Systems und Verification Engineering sowie mit der Fertigung zusammen.
 Diese Rolle passt zu dir, wenn du gerne Probleme löst, Systeme in der Tiefe verstehen willst und dir eine technische Expert*innenrolle wünschst.
 Deine Aufgaben
 Designs: Du entwickelst neue und überarbeitest bestehende Designs unserer Metallsensoren und Kameras, etwa wegen Abkündigungen, Kosten oder Verbesserungen aus dem Feld. Dazu gehören Schaltplan, Layout und Tests.
 Tests für die neue Kamera: Für unsere neue Hyperspektralkamera, die gerade auf den Markt kommt, entwickelst du Board- und System-Level-Tests und Testaufbauten für die Fertigung.
 Bauteile & Lebenszyklus: Du beobachtest Abkündigungen, findest Alternativen und Second Sources und hältst die Stücklisten im ERP aktuell.
 Fehleranalyse: Du gehst Auffälligkeiten aus Produktion und Feld systematisch auf den Grund und leitest Maßnahmen ab, die dauerhaft wirken. Für die Fertigung bist du die/der Second-Level-Support.
 Änderungen sauber umsetzen: Du bringst technische Änderungen durch Review, Freigabe und Fertigung, gemeinsam mit der Fertigungsabteilung, Einkauf und Qualität.
 Wissen sichern: Du dokumentierst Designs, Entscheidungen und Testergebnisse so, dass andere darauf aufbauen können.
 Das bringst du mit
 Eine technische Ausbildung in Elektronik oder Elektrotechnik (FH, TU oder vergleichbar)
 Mehrjährige Praxis in der Hardwareentwicklung, auch mit der Überarbeitung bestehender Designs und mit Produkten in der Serie
 Sicherheit in Analog- und Mixed-Signal-Schaltungstechnik, im Schaltplan- und Layoutdesign sowie im EMV- und ESD-gerechten Design
 Einen strukturierten Weg zur Fehlerursache: Du arbeitest gerne im Labor mit Oszilloskop, Logic Analyzer und Co. und gibst dich nicht mit dem ersten Symptom zufrieden
 Erfahrung mit Sensorik und Signalaufbereitung
 Erfahrung in der Bauteilauswahl mit Blick auf Verfügbarkeit, Lebenszyklus und Kosten
 Du übernimmst Projekte eigenständig, priorisierst selbst und holst dir Input, wenn es ihn braucht
 Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
 Nice to have
 Erfahrung mit Altium Designer
 Python und/oder C/C++ für Messskripte, Testaufbauten oder Debugging
 Erfahrung mit Gerätedesign auf Mechanik- und Elektronikebene
 Stücklistenpflege im ERP sowie Erfahrung mit Git und Jira
 Das erwartet dich
 Produkte, die du in der Tiefe kennenlernst und langfristig verantwortest
 Echte Eigenständigkeit und kurze Wege zu Firmware, Mechanik, Systems Engineering und Fertigung
 Eine Expert*innenrolle mit Zeit für gründliche Arbeit statt ständig neuer Projekte
 38,5-Stunden-Woche, Gleitzeit ohne Kernzeit, 1–2 Tage Homeoffice pro Woche
 Individuelle Weiterbildung
 Essenszuschuss, Zuschuss zum steirischen Klima-Ticket, kostenloser Parkplatz, Zukunftsvorsorge
 Über Headwall
 Headwall entwickelt innovative hyperspektrale Bildverarbeitungslösungen für industrielle und wissenschaftliche Anwendungen weltweit. An unserem Standort in Graz arbeiten wir in einem internationalen Umfeld an Technologien, die Ressourcen effizienter nutzen und nachhaltige Entscheidungen ermöglichen.
 So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess
 Wir sehen uns deine Unterlagen an und melden uns innerhalb von 1–3 Tagen, manchmal mit einem kurzen Videocall.
 Persönliches Kennenlernen im Office mit Patrick Verbeek, Head of Product Development, Claus Hohensinn, TechLead Hardware & PO Metal Sensors, und Manuela Rosenzopf-Dietl, People & Culture.
 Ein praktischer Teil: Wir schauen uns gemeinsam eine Baugruppe oder einen Schaltplan an und sprechen darüber, wie du an eine Fehleranalyse herangehst.
 Du lernst das Team, das Labor und die Fertigung kennen.
 Wir halten dich laufend über den Stand am Laufenden.

Qui sommes-nous ? 
 Fondée en 2014, Artefact est une société internationale de services autour de l'IA et de la data, spécialisée dans le conseil en IA, transformation data et en data & digital marketing. L’approche unique d’Artefact, qui fait le pont entre la donnée et le business, permet à nos clients d’atteindre leurs objectifs business de façon dédiée et efficace. Nos 2500 collaborateurs répartis dans 27 bureaux à travers le monde allient leurs compétences pluridisciplinaires au profit de l’innovation business des entreprises. 
 La mission des Artefactors ? Transformer la data de nos clients en impact business. Dans ce sens, nous collaborons avec plus de 1000 clients, leaders de leurs industries (Orange, Carrefour, Samsung, AccorHotels, L’Oréal, LVMH, Decathlon) et sommes partenaires privilégiés de Google (GMP/GCP), AWS ainsi que Microsoft Azure. 
 En tant que stagiaire Software Engineer, tu seras ammener à:  
 Participer activement à la conception et à l'implémentation de solutions techniques robustes et scalables.
 Architecture logicielle : Contribuer à la réflexion sur l'architecture de nos applications, en veillant à la performance et à la maintenabilité du code
 Déploiement et opérations (DevOps) :   automatisation des tests et des déploiements cloud avec des pipelines CI/CD et une infrastructure en tant que code (ex : Terraform), packaging d'applications dans des conteneurs (ex : Docker), implémentation d'outils d'observabilité des données (ex : DBT)
 Déploiement de ton logiciel sur le cloud  : GCP, AWS ou Azure 
 Déploiement d’une ou plusieurs expertises techniques suivantes : développement logiciel, ingénierie analytique, ingénierie ML, architecture cloud ou ingénierie de sécurité et de fiabilité des sites
 Veille technologique : Explorer de nouvelles technologies et outils pour optimiser nos méthodes de travail.
 Profil recherché 
 Formation : Tu es étudiant(e) en dernière année de cycle ingénieur, Master 2, ou équivalent, avec une spécialisation en sotware engineering, génie logiciel, informatique, ou développement web et tu recherches ton stage de fin d’études à partir de Janvier 2027
 Compétences techniques : 
 Maîtrise d'un ou plusieurs langages de programmation comme Python, Java, JavaScript (Node.js), Go ou Scala.
 Connaissance des principes de la programmation orientée objet et/ou de la programmation fonctionnelle.
 Expérience avec des bases de données SQL ou NoSQL.
 Une familiarité avec le Cloud (GCP, AWS, Azure) et les conteneurs (Docker, Kubernetes) est un atout.
 Connaissance des outils de versioning, en particulier Git .
 Qualités personnelles : 
 Curiosité et proactivité : Tu as envie d'apprendre et de proposer de nouvelles idées.
 Rigueur et souci du détail : Tu es soucieux(se) de produire un code propre et de qualité.
 Esprit d'équipe : Tu es capable de travailler en collaboration et d'échanger avec des profils variés (Data Scientists, Consultants, etc.)
 Français courant pour travailler en équipe et anglais professionnel obligatoire pour nos clients internationaux   
 Le processus de recrutement : pour rejoindre Artefact, nous te proposons un processus de recrutement en quatre étapes durant lequel tu auras l’occasion de parler de ton expérience et d'en apprendre davantage sur Artefact et le poste d'ingénieur logiciel.
 Entretien RH
 Entretien #1 – Test de codage avec un Senior Software Engineer 
 Entretien #2 - Test d'architecture et de pipeline avec un Senior Software Engineer 
 Entretien #3 - Entretien de motivation avec un Manager ou Directeur du pôle Data Engineering 
 Processus d'onboarding :  
 L'intégration comprend une formation sur des compétences transversales critiques telles que la gestion du temps, la communication orale et écrite. Un counsellor te sera également attribué qui te guidera dans ta familiarisation avec la culture et les méthodes de travail de l'entreprise. De plus, tu auras l'opportunité de travailler sur des projets internes pour acquérir une expérience pratique et perfectionner tes compétences. De plus, tu auras la possibilité d'obtenir des certifications sur les fournisseurs cloud avant de travailler sur des missions clients. Ce processus d'intégration est conçu pour te doter des connaissances et des compétences nécessaires pour devenir un ingénieur logiciel performant chez Artefact.
 Ce que nous offrons 
 Un stage de 6 mois basé à Paris .
 Un environnement de travail stimulant, où tu seras encouragé(e) à prendre des initiatives.
 Un accompagnement par un mentor expérimenté pour te faire progresser rapidement.
 L'opportunité de travailler sur des projets variés et complexes.
 La possibilité d'être embauché(e) en CDI à la fin du stage.
 Prêt à rejoindre l'aventure ? 
 Si tu te reconnais dans cette description et que tu souhaites mettre tes compétences au service de projets concrets et impactants, envoie-nous ta candidature !
 Chez Artefact, nous recrutons nos collaborateurs uniquement en fonction de nos besoins et des qualités propres de chaque candidat. Nous assurons le développement de leurs compétences professionnelles et de leurs responsabilités sans discrimination d’aucune sorte. Le groupe s'engage à reconnaître et promouvoir tous les talents, quels que soient leurs croyances, âge, handicap, parentalité, origine ethnique, nationalité, identité de genre, orientation sexuelle, appartenance à une organisation politique, religieuse, syndicale ou à une minorité, ou toute autre caractéristique qui pourrait faire l'objet d'une discrimination.

 Synopsys is a leader in silicon-to-systems engineering solutions, helping customers accelerate innovation in AI-driven products through industry-leading EDA, IP, and design solutions. 
 You Are 
 As a Principal Front-End Design Engineer, you will lead methodology, subsystem architecture, and AI-enabled design innovation across IP and SoC development. You will build scalable design solutions, improve engineering productivity, and drive best practices across global teams. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Develop and deploy AI-driven solutions for verification, synthesis, constraints, and DFT workflows. 
 Architect reusable subsystem reference designs for Synopsys IP. 
 Debug and optimize front-end design methodologies and automation flows. 
 Drive adoption of best practices across design and verification teams.

items.jobTitle: Elektroplaner Smart Home als Content Creator (m/w/d)
items.jobDescription:
Remote · 4-Tage-Woche möglich · 50.000–80.000 € p. a. (Vollzeit) 
 „Smart Home oder konventionell?“ Die Frage landet immer bei dir, weil du dich sehr gut auskennst und auch gut erklären kannst? Dann komm zu uns und mach genau das zu deinem Job!
 JETPLAN entwickelt die Zukunft der Elektroplanung – für Elektrohandwerk, Planer und Bauwirtschaft.
 Wir suchen eine Person, die echte Planungspraxis aus dem Wohnbau mitbringt und daraus Videos, Musterplanungen und How-tos für YouTube und Social Media macht. Du bist das Gesicht, das zeigt, wie moderne und zunehmend KI-gestützte Elektroplanung mit JETPLAN funktioniert.
 Dein Fachwissen ist dabei der Kern: Nur wer selbst plant, kann komplexe Themen so erklären, dass Elektriker und Bauherren wirklich etwas davon haben.
 Deine Aufgaben
 Du produzierst How-to-Videos, Tutorials und Kurzformate für YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram & Co. Dabei erklärst du, wie typische Kundenwünsche in JETPLAN planerisch dargestellt werden.
 Du erstellst normkonforme Musterplanungen für typische Wohnbauprojekte – vom Einfamilienhaus bis zur Wohnung, konventionell und Smart Home.
 Du zeigst Systeme wie KNX, Loxone und DALI im Planungsalltag: Wann passt was, worauf kommt es an?
 Du entwickelst Themen- und Formatideen mit und greifst Fragen aus der Community auf.
 Mit deiner Planungserfahrung bringst du wertvolle Impulse in die Produktentwicklung ein.
 Dein Publikum: Elektriker, Planer und planungsinteressierte Bauherren.
 Wohin die Rolle wachsen kann
 Im Kern geht es ums Planen, Erklären und Beraten vor der Kamera. Wenn du Lust und Erfahrung mitbringst, kann die Rolle deutlich strategischer werden: Du gestaltest die Content-Ausrichtung mit – welche Zielgruppen, welche Themen, wo Longform, wo Shortform –, spielst Inhalte gezielt über YouTube, Suche und Social Ads aus und wertest aus, welche Inhalte wirklich Anfragen bringen. Wie weit das geht, entscheiden wir gemeinsam – je nachdem, was du mitbringst.
 Das bringst du mit
 Du musst nicht aus einem Planungsbüro kommen: Quereinsteiger mit elektrotechnischer Ausbildung sind herzlich willkommen, vor allem aus dem Elektrohandwerk.
 Das ist uns wichtig
 Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Planung von Elektroinstallationen, konventionell und Smart Home, mit Schwerpunkt Wohnbau (komplexe Anlagen, Zweckbau oder Industrie musst du nicht beherrschen)
 Sichere Kenntnisse gängiger Systeme wie KNX, Loxone, DALI etc.
 Du kannst gut beraten und Zusammenhänge einfach erklären
 Du stehst gern vor der Kamera, nimmst dich ohne Scheu beim Planen auf und hast eine natürliche Präsenz
 Echte Freude an Elektroplanung und Smart Home
 Fließendes Deutsch (zwingend)
 Schön, aber kein Muss
 Kenntnisse in der Lichtplanung
 Gute Englischkenntnisse
 Erfahrung mit Videoaufnahme und Videoschnitt
 Eigene Kanäle oder erste Content-Erfahrung auf YouTube oder Social Media
 Erfahrung mit Content-Strategie, SEO oder Performance-Marketing
 Das bieten wir
 100 % remote: Du arbeitest von dort, wo du am besten planst und aufnimmst.
 4-Tage-Woche möglich: Mehr Zeit für dich – bei gleichem Anspruch an deine Arbeit.
 Gehalt: 50.000–80.000 € brutto pro Jahr bei 100 %, je nach Qualifikation
 Gestaltungsspielraum: Du prägst Formate und Inhalte von Anfang an mit – und wenn du willst, auch die gesamte Content-Ausrichtung.
 Kurze Wege: Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Gründerteam, Entscheidungen fallen schnell – ohne Politik, allein danach, was unseren Kunden wirklich hilft.
 KI-Planung von Anfang an: Du arbeitest mit den neuesten Planungswerkzeugen und prägst, wie sie im Alltag funktionieren.
 Bewirb dich – gern mit Video
 Du brennst für Elektroplanung? Wir freuen uns auf dich! Nutze den Bewerben-Button auf dieser Seite, um uns deinen Lebenslauf, deine Gehaltsvorstellung und deinen frühesten Starttermin zu senden.
 Statt eines Anschreibens freuen wir uns über ein kurzes Video (freiwillig, 1–3 Minuten, Handy reicht): Stell dich vor und erklär uns ein Smart-Home-Thema deiner Wahl – zum Beispiel, wann du KNX und wann Loxone empfiehlst. Falls vorhanden, verlinke gern Arbeitsproben oder eigene Kanäle.

Why Harvey 
 At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
 This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.
 Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
 At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
 Role Overview 
Harvey's Custom Solutions team builds tailored AI tools for leading strategic customers. The team scopes, designs and implements custom agents, playbooks and prompts to address high-priority use cases. Each solution is built around a customer's specific needs and stored in its Harvey instance for scalable access across the organization. Team members have opportunities to travel onsite and build relationships with senior stakeholders to support the rollout of these tools. They also partner with Harvey's Go-to-Market and Product teams to advance the platform by gathering feedback, surfacing opportunities and piloting features.
 What You'll Do 
 Establish a clear understanding of Harvey's platform and the process for building solutions (you're not expected to be a platform expert on day one, but you should be interested in becoming one).
 Scope, design and build custom agents, playbooks and prompts for key strategic customers.
 Build strong relationships with senior stakeholders to understand their requirements, map their processes and turn needs into working solutions.
 Prototype, test and iterate, including piloting Harvey features prior to general release.
 Communicate market feedback to Product and Engineering, surfacing the opportunities for enhancements that will be most impactful.
 Partner with Harvey's other Legal Engineering and Go-to-Market teams to deliver measurable growth.
 Create and maintain reusable assets, capturing best practices to speed up future deployments.
 What You Have 
 Qualified lawyer in England & Wales
 3+ years of experience as a practicing lawyer at a top-tier firm and/or in-house legal team.
 Curiosity about testing various approaches, evaluating deliverable quality and optimizing for customer outcomes and experience.
 Strong communication skills and a track record of partnering with senior stakeholders to drive results.
 Interest in driving positive change in the legal industry through AI.
 Experience using AI tools in legal practice is a plus.

Jobbeschreibung
 Die XIAO Gruppe ist eine mittelständische, inhabergeführte Unternehmensgruppe aus Gastronomie und Immobilienwirtschaft mit Sitz in Gelsenkirchen und Leverkusen. In unseren XIAO Restaurants in NRW begrüßen wir jedes Jahr rund 2 Millionen Gäste – getragen von knapp 1.000 Mitarbeitenden. Und wir wachsen weiter: In den kommenden drei Jahren wollen wir unseren Gastronomieumsatz verdoppeln, weitere Neueröffnungen stehen bereits fest.
 Damit unsere Restaurants und Verwaltung auch im Wachstum reibungslos arbeiten, suchen wir für unseren Standort Leverkusen zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Vollzeit einen IT-Systemadministrator (m/w/d) mit Schwerpunkt Microsoft 365 und 1st Level Support. Unsere IT-Infrastruktur ist cloudbasiert und bietet eine solide und geordnete Grundlage, die wir kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln. – Sie steigen in einen geordneten Betrieb ein, nicht in einen Dauer-Feuerwehreinsatz.
 Ihre Rolle bei uns:
 Gemeinsam mit unserer IT-Fachbereichsleitung und einem langjährigen externen IT-Partner stellen Sie den zuverlässigen Betrieb unserer IT sicher. Sie übernehmen eigenständig Aufgaben im IT-Support, in der Microsoft-365-Administration und in der Betreuung unserer standortübergreifenden IT-Infrastruktur. Außerdem vertreten Sie die Fachbereichsleitung bei Abwesenheit fachlich und organisatorisch.

 Einen unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag in Vollzeit in einer wachsenden Unternehmensgruppe
 Grundsätzlich keine Rufbereitschaft; nur in begründeten Ausnahmefällen, etwa bei Urlaubsvertretungen oder Neueröffnungen
 Eine attraktive, überdurchschnittliche Vergütung
 Feste Arbeitszeiten
 Fachliche Weiterentwicklung in einer modernen, cloudbasierten IT-Infrastruktur sowie die Möglichkeit zu Fortbildungen
 Ein kleines Team, kurze Entscheidungswege und einen direkten Draht zur Fachbereichsleitung
 Einen modern ausgestatteten Arbeitsplatz in einem klimatisierten Büro
 Verpflegung während der Arbeitszeit in unseren XIAO-Restaurants sowie kostenlose Getränke wie Wasser, Kaffee und Tee
 Regelmäßige Teamevents und Corporate Benefits
 Fahrtkostenzuschuss oder ein Jobticket möglich
 Kostenlose Parkmöglichkeiten
 Moderne IT-Ausstattung nach Wahl: Apple oder Lenovo sowie ein Diensthandy
 DAS KÖNNTE DEIN AUFGABENGEBIET SEIN 
 Sie administrieren und pflegen unsere Microsoft-365-Umgebung – insbesondere Entra ID, Intune, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint und SharePoint – sowie weitere cloudbasierte Systeme und entwickeln diese weiter.
 Sie begleiten unsere Neueröffnungen aktiv und sorgen vor Ort für den Anschluss und die Inbetriebnahme sämtlicher IT-Systeme.

 Sie unterstützen bei der Beschaffung von Hard- und Software und beraten technisch – gemeinsam mit unseren weiteren Supportbereichen.
 Sie steuern externe Dienstleister, unter anderem für unser Kassensystem, unsere 3CX-Telefonanlage, UniFi und Alarmtechnik.
 Sie schulen Mitarbeitende in technischen Anwendungen und sind für Restaurants und Fachabteilungen eine serviceorientierte Ansprechperson.
 Sie sind regelmäßig in unseren Betrieben in NRW vor Ort – die Fahrten finden innerhalb Ihrer Arbeitszeit statt.
 Stellenanforderungen

Sie wollen an innovativen Maschinen arbeiten und diese zum Leben erwecken?
 Als Service-Ingenieur:in / Inbetriebnehmer:in nehmen Sie unsere Anlagen bei uns im Hause zum ersten Mal in Betrieb. Bei Rückfragen unterstützt Sie ein kompetentes Team aus unterschiedlichen Fachabteilungen. Nach erfolgreicher Kundenabnahme folgen Sie der Anlage zum jeweiligen Bestimmungsort und führen dort, unter Berücksichtigung der örtlichen Gegebenheiten, die Wiederinbetriebnahme durch.
 Sie übernehmen nach Einarbeitung bereits früh Verantwortung für die Inbetriebnahme, Wartung und Montage unserer innovativen Prüf- und Produktionseinrichtungen
 Sie sind Teil unseres Serviceteams und unterstützen Ihre Kollegen bei der Weiterentwicklung unserer Prüfanlagen
 Sie erweitern Ihre interkulturelle Kompetenz bei der Betreuung unserer Kunden im In- und Ausland
 Sie arbeiten eng mit unseren Kunden zusammen und begeistern diese für unsere Produkte
Ausbildung: Sie besitzen ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Elektrotechnik oder Mechatronik. Eine Ausbildung als Elektroniker oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung ist von Vorteil
 Persönlichkeit: Sie sind offen, kommunikativ und haben Freude an der Arbeit im Team und am Kontakt mit Kunden
 Arbeitsweise: Sie arbeiten eigeninitiativ, analytisch und strukturiert
 Erfahrungen und Know How: Erfahrung in der Inbetriebnahme ist von Vorteil, gute Kenntnisse in der Elektrotechnik sind unbedingt erforderlich
 Begeisterung: Sie begeistern sich für innovative technische Lösungen und internationalen Serviceeinsätzen bei unseren Kunden
 Sprachen: Sie können sich sehr gut in deutscher (mindestens C1) und gut in englischer Sprache verständigen
Weltweit vertrauen die erfolgreichsten Unternehmen der Automobilbranche bei der Entwicklung, Produktion und Qualitätskontrolle von Antriebssystemen und Komponenten auf unsere moderne Prüftechnik für Elektrolyse, Brennstoffzellen, Diesel- und Benzineinspritzsysteme, Wasserstoffantriebe sowie für Hydraulikkomponenten.
 Vielfalt und Inklusion sind für uns keine Trends, sondern fest verankert in unserer Unternehmenskultur. Daher freuen wir uns über alle Bewerbungen: unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Behinderung, Religion, ethnischer Herkunft oder sexueller Identität.

items.jobDescription:
The EMBL Imaging Centre is seeking a Mechatronic Engineer to join our technology development activities at the interface of engineering, robotics and cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM).
 Two unique prototype instruments, EasyGrid and EasyGrid Control , have recently been deployed at the EMBL Imaging Centre in Heidelberg, enabling the automated preparation and quality control of samples for cryo-electron microscopy and cryo-electron tomography. The instruments combine multi-axis robots, light and holographic microscopy, cryogenic storage systems, an atmospheric plasma generator, and humidity- and temperature-controlled compartments.
 You will play a central role in the development of EasyGridNext , a next-generation platform for automated and reproducible cryo-EM sample preparation and dynamic on-grid experiments. Building on the established prototype systems, you will help develop them into a robust, service-ready platform that can be used reliably by researchers across the life sciences.
 The position offers the opportunity to apply your engineering expertise to challenging problems in structural and cellular biology. You will contribute to the complete development cycle, combining mechanical and electronic engineering, robotics, sensors and actuators, fluid handling, software-controlled instrumentation and cryogenic workflows , while collaborating directly with scientists who use these technologies to address biological questions.
 The role will be based within the EMBL Imaging Centre and will involve close collaboration with the EasyGrid development team at EMBL Grenoble , as well as researchers at EMBL and Heidelberg University.
 We are seeking a motivated and curious mechatronics engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems, learning new technologies and developing innovative, robust solutions to challenging engineering problems.
 Responsibilities 
 Lead and contribute to the engineering development and implementation of EasyGridNext , with a focus on reliability, robustness and service readiness.
 Design, prototype, integrate and test mechatronic subsystems , including microfluidic handling, temperature and humidity control, cryogenics, as well as a range of sensors and actuators.
 Contribute to the integration of hardware, software and experimental metadata into reliable and traceable workflows.
 Implement modular hardware for time-resolved fluid delivery and the study of dynamic biochemical reactions .
 Work with biological researchers to translate experimental requirements into engineering specifications and practical solutions .
 Contribute to the transition of prototypes into documented, maintainable and user-facing scientific infrastructure .
 Support the deployment of the resulting technology within the EMBL Imaging Centre and, ultimately, its use by the wider scientific community.
 Skills, Experience and Qualifications 
 You have 
 A degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Automation Engineering or a related engineering discipline , or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
 Practical experience in instrument development, mechatronic systems, motion control, machine vision, robotics or automation .
 A good understanding of relevant physical principles , including temperature, humidity, cryogenics, microfluidics, pneumatics, etc.
 Experience with CAD, rapid prototyping, machining or additive manufacturing .
 Strong problem-solving skills and a practical, hands-on approach to developing and improving complex technical systems.
 The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with scientists and engineers from different disciplines.
 Excellent communication and organisational skills , with the ability to translate scientific requirements into technical specifications and practical engineering solutions.
 You may also have 
 Experience in developing robotic or automated laboratory equipment .
 Experience with software development for scientific instrumentation , user interface development or object-oriented programming (e.g. Java).
 Experience in fluidics, precision dispensing or microfluidic systems .
 A background in cryo-EM or life sciences is not required . We particularly welcome candidates who bring strong engineering expertise and are interested in applying their skills to cryogenic sample preparation and advanced cryo-EM applications .
 Contract duration: 2 years
 Work schedule: This position is available exclusively on a part-time basis at 75–85% of full-time hours (approximately 29–33 hours per week, based on a 39-hour working week).
 Salary: Grade 6, monthly starting salary of €3.534,90–€4.006,22 after tax for a 75–85% part-time schedule, plus generous benefits and financial allowances based on individual circumstances. Excluding 12.99% personal pension and insurance contributions.
 Application process 
 We look forward to receiving your application. Please submit your CV and a cover letter through our online application system.
 In your cover letter, we invite you to describe how your engineering experience, technical expertise and approach to problem-solving could contribute to the development of next-generation instrumentation for cryo-electron microscopy and biological research . Candidates from engineering backgrounds who do not have previous experience in cryo-EM are encouraged to apply.
 The selection process will consist of two interview stages . Shortlisted candidates will first be invited to an online interview following the application deadline . Candidates progressing to the second stage will then be invited for an on-site interview.
 Further information about the position can be obtained from Simone Mattei (simone.mattei@embl.de).
 Why join us 
EMBL is curiosity-driven, community-oriented and international. As an inclusive, equal opportunity employer, we believe that diversity enables us to collaborate more effectively and be innovative in our approaches. We are, therefore, committed to creating an inclusive and flexible culture - one where everyone can realise their full potential and make a positive contribution to our organisation. 
 We encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing team – we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and personal experiences reflect the diversity of the populations that our science serves. We actively encourage applications from all genders and cultures, ethnic groups and all demographics to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights at this transformational point in our people strategy.
 Enjoy lots of benefits: 
 Financial incentives:  Salary free of income tax, Monthly family, child and non-resident allowances, annual salary review, pension scheme, death benefit, accident-at-work and unemployment insurances
 Flexible working arrangements 
 Private medical insurance  for you and your immediate family (including all prescriptions and generous dental & optical cover)
 Generous time off:  30 days annual leave per year, in addition to public holidays
 Relocation package  including installation grant (conditions apply) 
 Campus life: Library, on-site cafeteria, casual dress code, extensive sports and social club activities (on campus and remotely)
 Family benefits: Kindergarten (Heidelberg), 10 days of child sick leave, generous paid maternity/parental leave and monthly family & child allowances
 Benefits for international newcomers:  Visa exemption, education grant for private schooling, financial support to travel back to your home country every second year and a monthly non-resident allowance.
 For detailed information please visit our employee benefits page here 
 What else you need to know 
 International applicants: We recruit internationally and successful candidates are offered visa exemptions. Visit our International Applicants page, to find out more.
 EMBL is a signatory of DORA. Find out how we apply DORA principles to our recruitment and performance assessment processes here .
 Diversity and inclusion: At EMBL, we believe that diverse teams drive innovation and scientific excellence. We encourage applications from candidates of all genders, identities, nationalities and/or any other diverse backgrounds. 
 How to apply: To apply please submit a cover letter and a CV through our online system. Applications will close at 23:59 CET on the date shown below. We aim to provide a response within two weeks after the closing date.
 Closing Date

 Du konzipierst modulare, skalierbare Testumgebungen und Test-Frameworks für die neueste Generation militärischer Software-Defined Radios (SDR) und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter.

 Du hast tiefgreifende Erfahrung im Umgang mit komplexen elektrischen Messgeräten und ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Schaltungsanalyse.
 Du hast bereits Test-Frameworks konzipiert und kennst moderne Testautomatisierungsstrategien aus der Praxis.
 Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich und strukturiert, bist ein echter Teamplayer, kommunizierst klar und setzt dich mit guten Argumenten durch.

items.jobDescription:
This is an Atlantic portfolio company. 
 What we're building 
 Factories run on machines that generate huge amounts of data, and almost none of it gets used. We're changing that. We build AI software that helps production engineers and operators turn machine data into answers: why a line is slowing down, what's causing scrap, and what to fix next. We're early and in stealth. Our two founders both held C-level roles at leading German robotics ventures. They have spent years bringing advanced technology onto real shop floors, and now they're hiring the founding core team.
 Your role & responsibility 
 You're the person who makes our product work in the real world. You go into a plant, figure out what's actually broken, connect the data, and stay until operators use the product every day without being asked. You'll work with everyone from the machine operator to the plant manager, and with IT and OT. You own each customer from the first conversation through rollout and expansion. Berlin or home-based in Germany, with regular time in Berlin with the team. You'll spend about 20% of your time at customer sites.
 What you'll do 
 Own deployments end to end: use-case definition, data onboarding, validation, rollout, training, and adoption
 Turn messy production problems into clear data, analytics, and solution requirements
 Onboard and validate machine, process, quality, and maintenance data from industrial systems
 Spot data problems that only make sense if you understand the machine behind them
 Build and validate KPIs, features, anomaly signals, calibration methods, and analytical workflows in Python and SQL, using statistics and time-series analysis
 Run the project with the customer and our commercial lead: plans, workshops, validation sessions, and success criteria
 Find the next machine, line, data source, or use case, and expand with it
 Bring what you learn in the field back to the product, so each deployment makes the platform better
 Help write the playbook for how we deliver, as the customer engineering team grows
 You might be a fit if you 
 Have worked hands-on with industrial machines and production processes, in manufacturing, automation, maintenance, quality, industrial engineering, or industrial data
 Know your way around PLCs, SCADA, MES, historians, production databases, quality systems, or OPC UA
 Use Python and SQL to answer questions, not just to write code
 Have worked with time-series data, KPIs, anomaly detection, or root-cause analysis
 Communicate as well on the shop floor as in the plant manager's office
 Like solving hard problems in automation and process engineering
 Take ownership, work independently, and are comfortable when things are ambiguous
 Are happy to travel to customer sites and have a driver's license
 Speak fluent German and English
 A degree is optional. A Meister, Techniker, vocational training, or real-world experience counts just as much. We care about what you can do.
 We're open to experienced people who can lead deployments on their own, and to exceptional earlier-career people with strong industrial experience who learn fast.
 This is not a desk job. It's hands-on and customer-facing, and you'll spend a lot of your time where the machines are.
 Why now 
 You'll be one of the first people in the company. You'll work directly with the founders and shape how we deliver to customers from day one. What you build here becomes the way we work. We'll tell you more about the company, the founders, and our backers in the first conversation.

Since early 2024, we've gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business, and through that to make a real dent in the world's carbon emissions and a far better experience for homeowners.
 We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Most of our product is a front end over hard physics (heat-loss calculations, hydronic design, LiDAR floor plans, compliance that has to be right), used by installers on a phone, with no signal, in a hurry. Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.
   🌲 About Spruce
 Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.
 We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.
 We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…
   🥖 The role
 You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:
 Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.
 Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.
 Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.
 Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.
 Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.
 You'll report to Steph , our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.
   🫵 About you
 We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have:
 Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there.
 Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile.

items.jobDescription:
This is an Atlantic portfolio company. 
 About Marentis 
 Marentis develops AI-supported software for manufacturing, robotics and complex automated machinery. We turn machine data and operational information into useful knowledge for troubleshooting, decision-making and automation. Our work connects sensor measurements, machine and robot states, quality data, alarms and expert knowledge. These problems require understanding both the data and its context: a fault may originate elsewhere in a production line, and similar symptoms can have different causes. We are a small, early-stage startup where individual contributions directly shape the product. We value curiosity, initiative and people who enjoy understanding difficult problems and making things work.
 The Role 
 We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Software Engineer with strong Python skills and sound technical judgment. You will own backend features from problem definition through implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance.
 After onboarding, you should be able to investigate unfamiliar production code and independently review Python/backend pull requests: understand intended behavior, question assumptions, assess tests and failure paths, and identify effects on the wider system.
 We actively encourage AI-assisted development. You remain responsible for understanding, verifying and maintaining the resulting software. We value demonstrated delivery, ownership and learning ability more than a fixed number of years in the industry.
 What You Will Do 
 Build backend services, APIs and SQL-backed data pipelines for industrial analytics, knowledge retrieval and agent workflows.
 Read and improve existing code, review pull requests, and make informed decisions about interfaces, data models, state and failure handling.
 Design meaningful unit, integration and end-to-end tests, supported by continuous integration.
 Test with representative machine data, recorded streams and simulated device inputs, including missing measurements, duplicate or out-of-order events, invalid values and connection failures.
 Reproduce bugs, inspect whether test assertions verify the intended behavior, and add useful regression coverage.
 Understand manufacturing users and equipment, contribute across integration and deployment, and communicate trade-offs and blockers early.
 What You Bring 
 Strong practical Python and backend engineering skills, supported by software you personally shipped and maintained.
 Independent code-review ability: you can investigate a change, assess correctness, maintainability and security, and justify whether it is ready to merge.
 Practical system-design judgment across APIs, SQL, database design, data validation, state management and concurrency where relevant.
 Strong testing and debugging skills: you choose useful test boundaries, construct representative data and investigate failures.
 Experience making imperfect operational, machine, sensor or similarly complex data trustworthy, with an interest in its industrial meaning and consequences.
 Resourcefulness: you learn unfamiliar code and technologies through documentation, small experiments, focused questions and feedback.
 Clear written and spoken English, constructive collaboration and reliable follow-through.
 We welcome different educational and professional paths. Direct manufacturing experience is especially useful; equivalent engineering depth from adjacent domains is also relevant.
 Particularly Relevant Experience 
 Bring depth in one or more of these areas; expertise in all of them is not expected.
 Machine data, analytics and machine learning: Time-series or sensor-data processing, curation, feature engineering, anomaly detection, condition monitoring or quality prediction. Explain how you handled timestamps, units, asset identity and data quality, and evaluated whether the result was useful.
 Knowledge graphs and retrieval: Entity and relationship modeling, graph or relational database design, provenance, versioning and conflicting information. Experience combining identifiers, aliases, lexical search and semantic retrieval, with evaluations of relevance and applicability.
 Agent systems and workflows: LLM tools, multi-agent coordination, orchestration, context and memory management, validation and failure recovery. Show how you evaluated quality, cost and latency, enforced permissions and chose appropriate execution boundaries.
 Industrial integration, robotics and automation: Connecting software with production equipment, robot cells or automated machinery through telemetry, device interfaces or protocols such as MQTT and OPC UA. Experience with simulators, physical-device testing and equipment-specific behavior is valuable. 
 Cloud deployment, containerization, observability and operating software across customer environments are also useful.

 Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response, and turn blameless postmortems into durable reliability improvements.

 Experience operating web crawlers, search infrastructure, or browser fleets at scale.
 Experience with distributed queues, backpressure, workload isolation, or multi-region recovery.

items.jobDescription:
Perplexity is hiring a Web Access Engineer for the Crawler team to build reliable fetching and rendering systems for AI-powered search. You'll work on freely available public web content, within site permissions and approved access policies, and develop the infrastructure that supplies content to downstream indexing and retrieval systems.
 Your focus will be diagnosing network errors, page-loading issues, and incomplete rendering. You'll trace problems from network protocols through client-side execution, distinguish technical failures from intentional access restrictions, and turn findings into production fixes that improve content quality and efficiency at scale.
 Responsibilities 
 Own fetching and rendering improvements end to end, from investigation through implementation and production rollout, partnering with crawler engineers and SREs.
 Investigate fetch and rendering failures across DNS, TLS, HTTP, caching, redirects, and client-side rendering, and classify root causes.
 Improve page loading, completion detection, and content capture to preserve relevant content and handle dynamic pages reliably.
 Ensure the crawler respects site-imposed access restrictions and rate limits, identifies itself clearly, and retries only transient technical errors.
 Build tools to reproduce failures, compare crawler output against expected page content, and turn findings into regression tests.
 Define metrics for fetching reliability, content completeness, and error classification, and use them to prioritize improvements.
 Qualifications 
 5+ years of software engineering experience in web infrastructure, browsers, CDNs, or crawling, with strong programming skills in at least one of Go, Python, Rust, or C++.
 Deep understanding of HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, including status semantics, caching, conditional requests, content encoding, and redirects; strong knowledge of TLS, DNS, cookies, and sessions.
 Understanding of CDN caching and content delivery, HTTP error handling, retry backoff, and server-defined rate limits.
 Knowledge of page lifecycle, network idle, service workers, client-side rendering, and shadow DOM; experience debugging JavaScript and fluency with Chrome DevTools, CDP, HAR files, curl, and packet captures.
 Comfort working independently when the path forward is not fully defined.
 Nice to have 
 Experience developing CDN, caching, or web performance systems.
 Experience operating crawlers, headless browsers, or distributed content-acquisition systems at scale.
 Contributions to a browser engine or JavaScript runtime.

Help make the world more hospitable 
 The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.
 You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.
 If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.
 About the role 
 Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:
 You will own the agents, skills and standards that let a tribe of product builders move quickly on payments without the architecture fragmenting. Hotels take payments across regions and through providers that each behave differently, and Payment Interfaces exists to give customers one coherent payment experience on top of several PSPs. Embedded payments at this depth is rare among European SaaS companies, so the problems here are ones few engineers get to work on.
 You will be a Staff Engineer in the Payment Interfaces team, part of the Fintech tribe. You will report to the Director of Product and Engineering, sit in the tribe’s leadership group, and work alongside product builders, other staff engineers and product managers. No one reports to you, so your influence comes from the architecture, tools and standards that other people choose to work in.
 The team integrates several PSPs depending on region and conditions. When integrations drift apart, builders slow down and quality suffers. This role exists to keep them coherent by encoding what good looks like into tools and agents, so every builder meets the standard by default.
 What you would do  
 Own the tribe’s engineering agents, skills and context, and encode architectural standards, review logic and quality gates into them so the standard is met by default.
 Build an AI first responder for customer tickets about payment issues, with clear rules for when it answers and when it hands over to a person.
 Stay hands-on for the hardest technical problems: migrations, system-wide refactors and long-lived architecture decisions across PSP integrations.
 Keep Payment Interfaces integrations coherent as PSPs and regional requirements change, collaborating with builders who own their own work.
 Coach builders and fix off-standard outcomes at the cause, so the lesson sticks.
 AI Fluency Level 4: in this role, that means you build the AI systems the tribe works in, not only use them. TL;DR: 
How people discover Lovable is being rebuilt in real time. They now find software through Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude and others, and nobody has the full playbook yet. We're looking for an SEO and AEO specialist who wants to write it for Lovable and turn that visibility into subscribers and revenue. You're technical enough to land your own code and agentic enough to build the tools you need with AI. One sprint you're fixing how lovable.dev gets crawled and rendered; the next you're shipping pages for our highest-intent searches, or an agent that tracks where Lovable shows up in AI answers. Your first instinct is always: will people and answer engines find this, and does it help us grow?
 Why Lovable? 
 Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
 We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
 Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
 The role 
 You'll own organic discoverability for Lovable. Answer engines come first, on top of a strong foundation in traditional search. You do the strategy, building and measurement, there's no queue between an insight and a live change.
 You'll build most of your tools, pages and agents on Lovable itself, and take what you learn straight to the product team. Millions of apps are published on Lovable and each one needs to be found too, so what works for lovable.dev should become better defaults and guides for our users.
 What we’re looking for 
 5+ years in SEO, AEO or organic growth on a user-facing web product at scale. Results you've driven count for more than years.
 Hands-on AEO. You've tracked how AI assistants mention and cite a brand, tested what moves it, and can show the results.
 Deep technical SEO. Rendering, crawling, indexing, structured data, sitemaps, canonicals and internal linking at scale. When something breaks, you find out why.
 Agentic by default. You use AI coding tools and LLM APIs to build agents, scripts and internal tools that automate audits, monitoring and reporting, without waiting on engineering.
 You land code. You know enough web fundamentals (HTML, JavaScript, React, APIs) to work in our codebase, get changes through review into production, and own them after launch. You don't need to be a senior software engineer.
 Strong with data. SQL, Search Console, log files, event tracking, and tests that tell you something real.
 Good content and product judgment. You know what makes a page worth citing and cut what isn't working.
 Motivated by the scoreboard: traffic, citations, subscribers, revenue.
 What you’ll do 
 In one sentence: you'll own how Lovable gets found across search engines and AI assistants, and build the site, systems and tools that turn that into growth.
 Set the organic roadmap. Decide where Lovable needs to show up across Google, AI Overviews and AI assistants, which topics and queries matter most, and what we leave alone.
 Own the technical health of lovable.dev . Rendering, crawling, indexing, site structure, internal links, structured data and speed are yours. Keep search traffic safe through relaunches and redesigns.
 Ship pages that win high-intent search. Use search demand, prompt data and competitor gaps to pick what to build and refresh, then ship hub pages, templates, comparisons and other page systems. Work with content and product marketing on what goes on them.
 Get Lovable cited beyond our own site. Find the forums, communities, publications and docs that AI answers lean on for our category, and work with community, PR and partnerships to earn a place there.
 Make experimentation cheap and fast. Build the setup that lets the team test page formats, technical changes and distribution ideas in days, keep a record of each test, and double down on what works.
 Build the tools search runs on. Replace manual audits, monitoring and reporting with automations and agents, ideally built on Lovable, with a person checking the work where accuracy matters.
 Own how we measure organic. Tie rankings, AI citations and organic traffic to subscribers and revenue in the warehouse, so we can invest in organic with the same confidence as paid. Say plainly where the data has gaps.
 Help Lovable apps get found. Work with product engineering on SEO and AEO defaults (metadata, social previews, sitemaps, rendering) for the apps our users publish, and share what works as guides.
 Share what you learn. Bring findings back to product, and share our results with users and the wider community.
 Keep it Lovable. Search should make the site better for people, never worse.
 Our tech stack 
 We're building with tools that both humans and AI love:
 Frontend: React
 Backend: Golang and Rust
 Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Many LLM providers
 DevOps & Tooling: Github Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)
 About your application 
 Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
 We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

items.jobDescription:
Als Arbeitgeber sind wir  PRO YOU – weil bei uns der  Mensch im Mittelpunkt steht . Wir übernehmen Verantwortung füreinander, schaffen kontinuierliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten und bieten ein Umfeld, das berufliches und persönliches Wachstum fördert - mit flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen. 
 Proalpha – ERP- und Business Applications  für den Mittelstand 
 Seit mehr als drei Jahrzehnten ist die Proalpha Group an 66 Standorten weltweit der digitale Sparringspartner der mittelständischen Wirtschaft. Die leistungsstarken ERP- und Business Applications bilden das digitale Rückgrat der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette von mehr als 17.500 Kunden weltweit – Unternehmen aus der industriellen Fertigung, dem Großhandel und weiteren Branchen. Dabei sorgt Proalpha für die intelligente Vernetzung und effiziente Steuerung aller geschäftskritischen Systeme und Kernprozesse – von AI und Data Analytics bis hin zum Supply Chain- und Human Capital Management. Zusammen mit unseren Gruppenunternehmen  erweitern wir auch Deine Karrieremöglichkeiten. Der Corporate Planner ist ein Produkt der Proalpha und bietet Lösungen für das operative und strategische Controlling, die integrierte Erfolgs- und Finanzplanung sowie die Konsolidierung. Ziel ist es, Unternehmen maximale Flexibilität für fundierte Entscheidungsfindungen bereitzustellen und sie so nachhaltig auf künftige Herausforderungen vorzubereiten.
 Du arbeitest in  Vollzeit an unserem Standort in Hamburg und einzelne Tage im Homeoffice . 
 Deine Aufgaben – contra boring, PRO YOU     
 Du übernimmst die erste Kontaktstrecke zu potenziellen Kunden und formst daraus belastbare Sales-Chancen mit Fokus auf das Produkt Corporate Planner. Help make the world more hospitable 
 The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.
 You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.
 If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.
 About the role 
 Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:
 You will own the agents, skills and standards that let a tribe of product builders move quickly on payments without the architecture fragmenting. Hotels take payments across regions and through providers that each behave differently, and Payment Interfaces exists to give customers one coherent payment experience on top of several PSPs. Embedded payments at this depth is rare among European SaaS companies, so the problems here are ones few engineers get to work on.
 You will be a Staff Engineer in the Payment Interfaces team, part of the Fintech tribe. You will report to the Director of Product and Engineering, sit in the tribe’s leadership group, and work alongside product builders, other staff engineers and product managers. No one reports to you, so your influence comes from the architecture, tools and standards that other people choose to work in.
 The team integrates several PSPs depending on region and conditions. When integrations drift apart, builders slow down and quality suffers. This role exists to keep them coherent by encoding what good looks like into tools and agents, so every builder meets the standard by default.
 What you would do  
 Own the tribe’s engineering agents, skills and context, and encode architectural standards, review logic and quality gates into them so the standard is met by default.
 Build an AI first responder for customer tickets about payment issues, with clear rules for when it answers and when it hands over to a person.
 Stay hands-on for the hardest technical problems: migrations, system-wide refactors and long-lived architecture decisions across PSP integrations.
 Keep Payment Interfaces integrations coherent as PSPs and regional requirements change, collaborating with builders who own their own work.
 Coach builders and fix off-standard outcomes at the cause, so the lesson sticks.
 AI Fluency Level 4: in this role, that means you build the AI systems the tribe works in, not only use them. You design the agents, skills and evaluations that builders rely on every day, make the engineering decisions about how they behave, and set the rules for when an AI answer can stand and when a person must step in.
 For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to “ AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates ” on Confluence. 
 What you would bring  
 Hands-on experience integrating with payment service providers or payment processors.
 Deep engineering craft and architectural judgment, including a sense of what is worth codifying and what is a one-off.
 AI Fluency Level 4 or the equivalent hands-on experience: you have built agents, skills, evaluations or tooling that other engineers use, and you can explain where human oversight stays non-negotiable.
 A systems mindset that turns hard-won knowledge into reusable architecture and tooling rather than documentation.
 Comfort with influence as your main way of getting things done, working with builders, product managers, principals and senior leaders without anyone reporting to you.
 Nice to have  
 Experience in hospitality, travel or another operationally complex B2B SaaS environment.
 Experience publishing or speaking externally about your work.
 A track record of coaching other engineers and multiplying their effectiveness.
